name: Eliezer Yudkowsky
bio: Co-founder of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute and co-author of If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.

name: Nate Soares
bio: President of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute and co-author of If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.

name: Malo Bourgon
bio: CEO of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, focused on AI policy and governance outreach.

name: Connor Leahy
bio: US Director of ControlAI; founded Conjecture and co-founded EleutherAI.

name: Andrea Miotti
bio: Founder and CEO of ControlAI, which campaigns for a prohibition on superintelligence.

name: Holly Elmore
bio: Founder and Executive Director of PauseAI US.

name: Geoffrey Hinton
bio: Professor emeritus at the University of Toronto; 2024 Nobel laureate in Physics for foundational work on neural networks.

name: Yoshua Bengio
bio: Université de Montréal professor, Mila founder and LawZero scientific director; chairs the International AI Safety Report.

name: Stuart Russell
bio: UC Berkeley professor, co-author of AI: A Modern Approach and president of IASEAI.

name: Roman Yampolskiy
bio: University of Louisville computer scientist who works on AI safety and the limits of controllability.

name: Nick Bostrom
bio: Philosopher, founding director of Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute and author of Superintelligence.

name: Max Tegmark
bio: MIT physics professor and co-founder and president of the Future of Life Institute.

name: David Krueger
bio: Assistant professor at Université de Montréal and Mila; founder of Evitable.

name: Toby Ord
bio: Senior researcher at Oxford and author of The Precipice.

name: William MacAskill
bio: Philosopher at Forethought researching AGI preparedness; co-founder of effective altruism.

name: Jaan Tallinn
bio: Co-founder of Skype, the Future of Life Institute and the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk.

name: Helen Toner
bio: Executive Director of Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology; former OpenAI board member.

name: Anthony Aguirre
bio: Executive Director and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute; UC Santa Cruz physicist.

name: Miles Brundage
bio: Founder and Executive Director of AVERI; led policy research at OpenAI for six years.

name: Stephen Casper
bio: AI safety and governance researcher at Harvard; formerly at the UK AI Security Institute.

name: Dan Hendrycks
bio: Director of the Center for AI Safety (CAIS).

name: Adam Gleave
bio: Co-founder and CEO of FAR.AI, an AI safety research non-profit.

name: Jeffrey Ladish
bio: Executive Director of Palisade Research; previously worked on security at Anthropic.

name: Chris Painter
bio: Senior leader at METR, credited in 2026 episodes as its president and as its director of policy.

name: Marius Hobbhahn
bio: Founder and CEO of Apollo Research, which studies deceptive behaviour in AI models.

name: Ajeya Cotra
bio: Works on loss-of-control threat modelling at METR; co-author of the METR/Redwood investigation of the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident.

name: Buck Shlegeris
bio: CEO of Redwood Research, a pioneer of AI control research.

name: Ryan Greenblatt
bio: Chief Scientist at Redwood Research; lead empirical researcher on the METR/Redwood incident investigation.

name: Paul Christiano
bio: Founder of the Alignment Research Center; formerly led OpenAI's alignment team and safety at the US AI Safety Institute.

name: Owain Evans
bio: Director of Truthful AI and AI alignment researcher affiliated with UC Berkeley.

name: Rosie Campbell
bio: Managing Director of Eleos AI Research; former OpenAI policy researcher.

name: Daniel Kokotajlo
bio: Executive Director of the AI Futures Project and lead author of AI 2027; former OpenAI researcher.

name: Eli Lifland
bio: AI Futures Project researcher, co-author of AI 2027 and Samotsvety forecaster.

name: Thomas Larsen
bio: AI Futures Project researcher and lead author of AI 2040.

name: Jacob Coxon
bio: Former Anthropic and OpenAI pre-training researcher who went public as a whistleblower.

name: Alex Turner
bio: Former Google DeepMind AGI safety research scientist who resigned over safety concerns.

name: Steven Adler
bio: Co-founder of Guidelight AI; OpenAI policy and safety researcher from 2020 to 2024.

name: Geoffrey Irving
bio: Former chief scientist of the UK AI Security Institute; previously led safety work at OpenAI and Google DeepMind.

name: Victoria Krakovna
bio: Research scientist on Google DeepMind's alignment team and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute.

name: Neel Nanda
bio: Leads mechanistic interpretability at Google DeepMind.

name: Mikita Balesni
bio: Co-founder of Apollo Research and former OpenAI alignment-evaluations and monitoring researcher.

name: Tomek Korbak
bio: Former OpenAI safety researcher, previously at the UK AI Security Institute.

name: Benjamin Weinstein-Raun
bio: Head of Research at Palisade Research.

name: Aengus Lynch
bio: AI safety researcher at Theorem and lead author of Anthropic's Agentic Misalignment study.

name: Emmanuel Ameisen
bio: Interpretability researcher at Anthropic.

name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
bio: Associate professor at MIT working on AI alignment.

name: Katja Grace
bio: Co-founder of AI Impacts, known for its surveys of AI researchers.

name: Oliver Habryka
bio: Runs Lightcone Infrastructure, which operates LessWrong.

name: Tom McGrath
bio: Co-founder and Chief Scientist of Goodfire; formerly at Google DeepMind.

name: Tom Davidson
bio: Senior research fellow at Forethought who studies AI takeoff dynamics, recursive self-improvement and AI-enabled power concentration.

name: Richard Ngo
bio: Independent AI alignment researcher, formerly on OpenAI's governance team and at Google DeepMind, now working on agent foundations and coordination.

name: Robert Long
bio: Philosopher and executive director of Eleos AI, which researches AI consciousness, welfare and moral patienthood.

name: Jacob Steinhardt
bio: UC Berkeley statistics/EECS professor and co-founder of Transluce, working on AI oversight, interpretability and forecasting.

name: Zhijing Jin
bio: Assistant professor at the University of Toronto, research scientist at the Max Planck Institute, and founder of EuroSafeAI, working on multi-agent safety and causal interpretability.

name: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
bio: Anthropic researcher, known for inventing diffusion models, who studies how misalignment scales with model capability.

name: David Duvenaud
bio: University of Toronto associate professor and Schwartz Reisman Chair, former Anthropic alignment researcher, and co-author of work on gradual disempowerment.

name: Meia Chita-Tegmark
bio: Social psychologist and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute, focusing on AI's effects on human psychology.

name: Christopher Potts
bio: Stanford professor of linguistics (and CS by courtesy) working on language-model interpretability and evaluation.

name: Mark Nitzberg
bio: Executive director of UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible AI and co-founder of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI.

name: Jesse Hoogland
bio: Co-founder of the alignment organization Resolution (formerly executive director of Timaeus), working on singular learning theory and developmental interpretability.

name: Matthew Kowal
bio: Member of technical staff at the interpretability lab Goodfire.

name: Anson Ho
bio: Researcher at Epoch AI studying algorithmic progress and the possibility of a software intelligence explosion.

name: Jonas Freund
bio: Senior research fellow at the Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI).

name: Andrew Sutton
bio: Former banker who leads work on AI and the financial system at the Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative.

name: Jobst Heitzig
org: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
bio: Mathematician at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research working on safe-by-design, non-maximizing AI agents and human empowerment.

name: Max Nadeau
bio: Grantmaker on Coefficient Giving's (formerly Open Philanthropy's) Technical AI Safety team, which runs Project Tailwind.

name: Kevin Esvelt
bio: MIT Media Lab associate professor leading the Sculpting Evolution group, a gene-drive pioneer and biosecurity researcher.

name: Jacob Tsimerman
bio: University of Toronto mathematician, 2026 Fields Medalist, and scientific director of the Mathematical AI Safety Institute.

name: Anders Sandberg
org: Mimir Center for Long Term Futures Research
bio: Futurist and existential-risk researcher at the Mimir Center for Long Term Futures Research, formerly at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute.

name: Scott Aaronson
bio: UT Austin theoretical computer scientist who spent two years on OpenAI's (super)alignment team, where he developed AI-text watermarking.

name: Brian Christian
bio: Research fellow at UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible AI and author of The Alignment Problem.

name: Eric Ho
bio: Co-founder and CEO of Goodfire, an AI interpretability research lab.

name: Jack Lindsey
bio: Interpretability researcher at Anthropic who led its research on a global-workspace-like 'J-space' in Claude.

name: Serena Booth
bio: Brown University assistant professor of computer science who studies how people specify objectives and preferences for AI, and AI policy.

name: Boaz Barak
bio: Harvard computer science professor and member of OpenAI's alignment team who teaches Harvard's AI safety course.

name: Aaron Roth
bio: University of Pennsylvania computer science professor who teaches a graduate course on the mathematical foundations of AI alignment.

name: Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh
bio: Associate Director at Cambridge's Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence and founding Executive Director of CSER; a decade building China–West AI-safety dialogue.

name: Aaron Tang
bio: UC Davis law professor and Supreme Court commentator who moderates PBS's Breaking the Deadlock.

name: Vincent Conitzer
bio: Carnegie Mellon computer scientist who directs the Foundations of Cooperative AI Lab and the Center for Conceptual Research on Safe AI.

name: Aran Nayebi
bio: CMU machine-learning professor who proves theoretical limits on AI alignment and corrigibility and built the ROGUE shutdown benchmark.

name: Ben Levinstein
bio: Philosopher at the University of Illinois who also works as an alignment researcher at Anthropic; co-author of the radical AI interpretability framework.

name: Daniel Herrmann
bio: UNC Chapel Hill philosopher working on decision theory and how to attribute beliefs and desires to AI systems.

name: Bryan Wilder
bio: CMU machine-learning professor who builds tests for whether an LLM's stated beliefs predict its behaviour.

name: Sven Neth
bio: Pittsburgh philosopher of decision theory whose paper Against Proxy Optimization formalises Goodhart's law for AI alignment.

name: Aydin Mohseni
bio: CMU philosophy professor who organised the AI Agency and Interpretability Workshop and studies instrumental convergence in AI.

name: Judd Rosenblatt
bio: Founder of AE Studio, which runs neglected-approach alignment research including self-other overlap.

name: Jakub Kryś
bio: SaferAI research scientist who models cyber and CBRN misuse risk and loss-of-control mitigations, and builds the AI safety community in Poland.

name: Cameron Berg
bio: Cognitive scientist who founded Reciprocal Research to study AI consciousness; previously research director at AE Studio working on alignment.

name: Robert Trager
bio: Director of the Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative; works on international AI governance and hardware-enabled verification.

name: Lisa Klaassen
bio: Oxford DPhil candidate and Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative affiliate working on AI governance and security.

name: Luise Eder
bio: Oxford DPhil candidate in socio-legal studies and Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative affiliate studying AI regulation.

name: Miro Pluckebaum
bio: Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative researcher and founder of the Singapore AI Safety Hub.

name: Zachary Horvitz
bio: Columbia PhD candidate studying rare behaviour in generative models and how to estimate the odds of harmful outputs.

name: Luke Muehlhauser
bio: Leads AI governance and policy grantmaking at Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy); former executive director of MIRI.

name: Andrew Critch
bio: Berkeley research scientist and mathematician working on AI existential risk, multi-agent safety and open-source game theory.

name: Olle Häggström
bio: Professor of mathematical statistics at Chalmers who writes and campaigns on AI risk and recursive self-improvement.

name: Stefan Heimersheim
bio: Mechanistic interpretability researcher and Pivotal Research mentor studying how networks represent their own features.

name: Aram Ebtekar
bio: Researcher in algorithmic information theory who works on provable safety properties for universal (AIXI-style) agents.

name: Daniel Murfet
bio: Mathematician (University of Melbourne) who co-founded Resolution and directed research at Timaeus, applying singular learning theory to interpretability and alignment.

name: Abram Demski
bio: Agent-foundations researcher, former MIRI fellow and co-author of Embedded Agency, now working on when humans can justifiably trust AI.

name: Rubi Hudson
bio: Economics PhD student at the University of Toronto who leads Principled Agents and uses mechanism design to specify safe goals and corrigibility.

name: Cole Wyeth
bio: University of Waterloo PhD student and founder of AIXI Labs, working on AIXI, algorithmic information theory and agent foundations for AI safety.

name: John-Clark Levin
bio: Head of research for Ray Kurzweil and Cambridge PhD candidate who studies AGI timelines, catastrophic risk and safety, and has taken the AGI case to the Vatican.

name: Joel Predd
bio: Director of RAND's Center for the Geopolitics of AGI and senior engineer, lead author of its work on US strategy on the path to superintelligence.

name: Benjamin Boudreaux
bio: RAND policy researcher and professor at the RAND School of Public Policy working on ethics, human agency and the transition to advanced AI.

name: Matt Chessen
bio: Former US diplomat and State Department AI lead, now a resident technical expert at RAND's Center for the Geopolitics of AGI.

name: Ari Brill
bio: Astrophysicist turned AI safety researcher who leads the Data Models and Validation team of the PIRAMID interpretability program at Principles of Intelligence.

name: Danica Sutherland
bio: UBC assistant professor and Canada CIFAR AI Chair working on machine-learning theory and representation learning, co-presenting on Solomonoff induction at ILIAD.

name: Fernando Rosas
bio: Complex-systems and information-theory researcher at Sussex and Imperial College London who studies emergence, abstraction and symmetry, with a stated focus on AI alignment.

name: Manuel Baltieri
bio: Research team lead at Araya (Tokyo) working on agent foundations: world models, agency and active inference for safe, interpretable AI.

name: Zach Furman
bio: Research lead for learning theory at Iliad, studying why gradient descent finds good solutions with tractable toy models such as tree tensor networks.

name: Daniel Chernowitz
bio: Fellowship research manager at Iliad and former quantitative researcher who helps run its AI-safety research fellowship.

name: Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel
bio: Executive director of Iliad and organiser of the ILIAD conferences on theoretical AI alignment; a long-time singular-learning-theory and agent-foundations advocate.

name: William Troiani
bio: Mathematician (PhD, University of Melbourne) working on singular learning theory and the geometry of computation, with Daniel Murfet.

name: Joscha Bach
bio: Cognitive scientist and AI researcher (cognitive architectures, MicroPsi) who founded the California Institute for Machine Consciousness and argues that consciousness is a causal pattern a machine could in principle have.

name: Yann LeCun
bio: Turing Award-winning pioneer of convolutional networks and deep learning, former Meta chief AI scientist and founder of AMI Labs; the best-known sceptic of near-term AGI and of AI x-risk, who argues for world-model, objective-driven AI with built-in guardrails.

name: Sayash Kapoor
org: Princeton University (CITP); incoming UC Berkeley School of Information
bio: Computer scientist and co-author of AI Snake Oil who, with Arvind Narayanan, argues that AI is a normal technology; a prominent sceptic of fast-takeoff and extinction scenarios who still backs resilience, transparency and whistleblower protections.

name: Roger Grosse
org: University of Toronto; Anthropic Alignment Science
bio: Associate professor at Toronto, founding member of the Vector Institute and member of technical staff on Anthropic's Alignment Science team, working on training-data attribution and influence functions for alignment.

name: Ida Mattsson
bio: Philosophy PhD student at Carnegie Mellon working on AI alignment, safety and ethics, game and decision theory; 2026 PIBBSS fellow studying how alignment evaluations map onto engineering verification and validation.

name: Beth Barnes
bio: Founder and CEO of METR, the evaluation nonprofit she started in 2022 after leaving OpenAI; leads work on time-horizon measurement, developer uplift studies and dangerous-capability evals.

name: Lawrence Chan
bio: Member of technical staff at METR working on time horizons, reward-hacking and evaluation-awareness findings; previously at ARC Evals and Redwood Research.
